# Starfighters Space F-104 Fleet Targeted for Hypersonic Interceptor Flight Tests Under Horizon Apogee MOU


November 16, 2026 9:00am EST


*Planned 2027 flight campaign to evaluate advanced high-speed vehicle and propulsion technologies through subsonic and supersonic testing*


KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--[Starfighters Space, Inc.](https://starfightersspace.com/) ("Starfighters" or the "Company") (NYSE American: FJET), the space company operating the world's only commercial fleet of flight-ready Mach 2+ supersonic aircraft, today announced the Company will work with[Horizon Apogee LLC](https://www.horizonapogee.com/) , an aerospace technology company specializing in advanced high-speed flight and propulsion systems, on a series of planned supersonic test flights to assess the design of Horizon Apogee’s Reaver™ hypersonic interceptor and its Orthrus™ combined-cycle air-breathing propulsion system. Horizon Apogee is developing Reaver under a *xTech|Search 10* competition funded by the US Army.


Starfighters and Horizon Apogee have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) outlining a 2027 flight-test campaign, with captive-carry flights planned for the second quarter and drop tests in the third quarter. The campaign would follow a vertical launch test of a Reaver prototype that Horizon Apogee plans to conduct early in 2027 at the Army’s White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico.


Under the MOU, Reaver would be carried beneath the wing of a Starfighter F-104 aircraft, allowing engineers to evaluate the vehicle's integration and performance under real-world flight conditions before progressing to drop testing. Pricing and terms for the flight phases are to be established in a definitive agreement the parties expect to negotiate before captive-carry flights begin.


“This project demonstrates how our existing Mach 2+ F-104 fleet can support the development of advanced aerospace and defense technologies,” said Tim Franta, CEO of Starfighters Space. “Companies developing hypersonic hardware need access to real-world flight conditions to evaluate their systems and reduce technical risk. Our fleet provides a specialized flight-testing platform that can support this development process.”


The proposed five-phase campaign would begin with aerodynamic integration analysis and aircraft fit checks, followed by flight readiness preparations. Subsequent phases would include subsonic and supersonic captive-carry flights and drop testing over an approved test range. The final phase would focus on reviewing flight data and evaluating potential follow-on activities, including powered flight testing.


“Moving Orthrus into a repeatable flight test environment is a major step for our program,” said Jason Kenney, CEO of Horizon Apogee. “Building on our subscale hot-fire test in June, flying Reaver on Starfighters’ F-104 will give us the flight data we need to retire key integration risks and move toward powered flight.”


The Orthrus propulsion system is being developed around a combined-cycle, air-breathing architecture intended to transition from ramjet to scramjet operation as vehicle speed increases.


**About Horizon Apogee LLC**


[Horizon Apogee LLC](https://www.horizonapogee.com/) is a Florida-based aerospace company developing the Orthrus™ family of combined-cycle, air-breathing hypersonic propulsion engines and the Reaver™ flight vehicle. The company completed a subscale hot-fire test in June 2026.


**About Starfighters Space, Inc.**


[Starfighters Space](https://starfightersspace.com/) (NYSE American: FJET) operates its fleet of F-104 aircraft at Kennedy Space Center in Florida and the Midland International Air & Space Port in Texas, making it the only company in the world with the commercial capability to fly at sustained Mach 2+ speeds, supporting a variety of aerospace applications. The iconic F-104 jets are configurable as a platform for air-launched payloads, training for pilots, and to support RDT&E (Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation) for hypersonic technologies, advanced materials, missile defense systems, microgravity science, spaceflight hardware validation, and defense electronic systems.
